problem.title: A Quarter More
problem.statement: A quantity increases from 80 by 25%. What is the new quantity?
hints: Twenty-five percent is one quarter of the original 80.

solutionSteps.title: Find and add the change
solutionSteps.body: 25% of 80 is 20, so the new quantity is 80 + 20 = 100. Equivalently, 80 × 1.25 = 100.

validationMethods: Change method: one quarter of 80 is 20, and 80+20=100.
Independent multiplier and option audit: 80×1.25=100; only C matches.

problem.title: Fifteen Percent Off
problem.statement: A $200 price is reduced by 15%. What is the new price?
hints: A 15% decrease leaves 85% of the original price.

validationMethods: Independent change subtraction: 15% of 200 is 30, and 200−30=170; only C matches.
notes: Choice A is the discount amount, separating change from final value.

problem.title: Two Different Discounts
problem.statement: An item is discounted 10% and then discounted 20% from its new price. What single percent discount from the original price is equivalent?
hints: Multiply the two percentages that remain.

solutionSteps.title: Compose remaining factors
solutionSteps.body: The item keeps 90% and then 80%: 0.90 × 0.80 = 0.72. It keeps 72%, so the total discount is 28%.

validationMethods: Independent $100 model: $10 is removed first, then $18 from $90, totaling $28; only B matches.
notes: The percentages differ from the bank problem and test transfer of the method.

problem.title: Recover the Starting Amount
problem.statement: After increasing by 25%, a quantity is 150. What was the original quantity?
hints: The final amount is 125% of the original, not 125% of itself.

solutionSteps.title: Undo the multiplier
solutionSteps.body: The increase multiplies the original by 1.25, so the original is 150 ÷ 1.25 = 120.

validationMethods: Independent forward check: 25% of 120 is 30 and 120+30=150; only C returns the final amount.
notes: The final amount is not reused as the original base.

problem.title: Points versus Percent Change
problem.statement: A survey response rate rises from 32% to 40%. What are the increase in percentage points and the relative percent increase, respectively?
hints: Subtract for points; compare that difference with the original 32% for relative change.

solutionSteps.title: Compute both meanings
solutionSteps.body: 40% − 32% = 8 percentage points. Relative to the original rate, 8/32 = 1/4 = 25%.

validationMethods: Independent 100-response model: responses rise from 32 to 40, an increase of 8; 8 is one quarter of 32, confirming 25%. Only C contains both values.
notes: Both requested measures and their order are explicit.
